battle.name: 第一次卡洛斯戰爭
battle.brief: 費爾南多七世一八三三年九月三十日病逝，四歲的伊莎貝拉二世即位，其弟卡洛斯親王起兵爭位，戰事在納瓦拉與巴斯克鄉土燒了七年，一八三三年十月雙方初次接觸，至一八三九年《維加拉公約》罷戰。卡面的輪發槍到此時已是淘汰品，只在軍官侍衛與王家衛隊手中留作象徵，實戰交火交給燧發步槍、火繩獵槍與火槍。

kit.name: 輪發槍
kit.history: 最早的後膛槍。機械太貴，只給火槍隊的軍官與衛兵。

countries: 第一次卡洛斯戰爭是西班牙自一八三三年末至一八四〇年的內戰，交戰一方是卡洛斯派，另一方是自由派。卡洛斯派以已故費爾南多七世之弟卡洛斯親王為正統旗幟，核心地帶是納瓦拉與巴斯克西部三省；當地教區神父的密度高於全國平均，基層神職人員替卡洛斯派做募兵、傳信與地方行政，軍隊骨幹是納瓦拉第三營，後來「雷克特斯」一詞泛指所有卡洛斯戰士，另有扎馬拉卡雷基組建的「海關民兵」，以及一八三四年阿爾薩蘇瓦戰役後由被俘自由派士兵改編成的「納瓦拉嚮導」；作戰單位多按村鎮編成游擊分隊，機動範圍廣，卻只有零星火炮，卡洛斯一方的最高權力機關是自己的「王國會議」，並在歐納提與維多利亞設鑄幣廠維持軍費。自由派一方由攝政王后瑪麗亞·克里斯蒂娜·波旁在馬德里執政，代表三歲的伊莎貝拉二世繼承王位，掌握首都、正規軍與主要港口；軍隊以王朝陸軍團、王家衛隊與國民警民兵為主，另組建巴斯克志願隊「沙佩爾戈里」。一八三四年《四國同盟條約》之後，英國派出德·拉西·埃文斯將軍率領的英國輔助軍團，法國外籍兵團以「西班牙兵團」之名參戰，葡萄牙派出安塔斯伯爵率領的常備師，海上則由西班牙與英葡艦隊封鎖比斯開灣沿岸。自由派握有稅收、造船與外國貸款，卡洛斯派握有鄉間與山區，兩邊的分野因此是「城對鄉」，也是「正規對游擊」。
countriesEn: The First Carlist War was a civil war fought in Spain from late 1833 to 1840, with the Carlists on one side and the Liberals on the other. The Carlists raised the banner of the rightful succession in the person of Carlos, Prince of Spain, brother of the late Ferdinand VII, and their heartland was Navarre together with the three western Basque provinces. The parish clergy there were denser than anywhere else in the country, and the lower clergy did the recruiting, the carrying of messages and the local administration for the Carlists. The backbone of their army was the Third Battalion of Navarre, after which the word requeté came to be used for all Carlist fighters; beside these stood the aduaneros raised by Zumalacárregui, the Guías de Navarra formed out of liberal soldiers captured at the battle of Alsasua in 1834, and a swarm of partisan bands organised village by village, wide-ranging in movement but possessed of only a handful of guns. The supreme organ of the Carlist side was its own Royal Council, and mints at Oñati and Vitoria struck coin to keep the bands in pay. On the other side the Liberals were governed from Madrid by the regent María Cristina of Bourbon, acting for the three-year-old Isabella II, and they held the capital, the regular army and the principal ports. Their forces were the dynastic line regiments, the Royal Guard and the national militia, supplemented by Basque volunteer units known as the chapelgorris. After the Quadruple Alliance treaty of 1834, Britain sent the British Auxiliary Legion under General de Lacy Evans, the French Foreign Legion campaigned in Spain under the name of the Spanish Legion, and Portugal sent a regular division under the Count of Antas, while Spanish, British and Portuguese warships blockaded the shore of the Bay of Biscay. The Liberals held the taxes, the shipyards and the foreign loans; the Carlists held the countryside and the mountains. The division between the two sides therefore ran along the line of town against country, and of regular army against partisan.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩邊。卡洛斯親王是名義上的領袖，但前期真正掌握戰場的是將軍托馬斯·德·扎馬拉卡雷基；此人是半島戰爭的老兵，曾在法軍中作戰，轉投卡洛斯一方後靠紀律與機動取勝，他宣誓擁護納瓦拉的自治法規，被推為納瓦拉總司令，比斯開、阿瓦瓦與吉普斯夸三省的省議會隨後宣誓服從他，他以阿梅斯科阿斯山區為大本營，據記錄曾有三千名毫無裝備的志願者前來投奔。扎馬拉卡雷基在比爾巴鄂攻城戰中被流彈傷及腿部，傷口久治不癒，最終死在一八三五年八月，他的死是北方戰局逆轉的關鍵。卡洛斯陣中還聚集了一批外籍冒險者與寫作者：英籍的亨寧森任他的侍衛長並後來撰寫傳記，什瓦岑貝格親王、利希諾夫斯基男爵等數十名歐洲人上過戰場，約二百五十名外國志願者多為法國王黨。自由派一方的樞紐是攝政王后瑪麗亞·克里斯蒂娜與幼主伊莎貝拉二世，馬德里先後由塞阿·貝爾穆德斯、馬丁內斯·德·拉·羅薩與托雷諾伯爵執政；將領中，瓦爾德斯多·德·奎薩達、馬塞利諾·德·奧拉阿是半島戰爭與南美獨立戰爭的老兵，耶羅尼莫·巴爾德斯參加過阿亞庫喬戰役，戰功卓著者還有利奧波爾多·奧多尼爾，最終扭轉北方戰局的是埃斯帕特羅，他接手後以果斷的縱隊作戰把卡洛斯派逐出北方。卡洛斯派一方也有拉法埃爾·馬羅托這個關鍵人物，他在一八三九年代表卡洛斯派簽訂和約；東線的拉蒙·卡布雷拉與阿里斯蒂斯陣營裡的卡洛斯派將領，則在莫雷利亞堅持到最後。整場戰爭裡還有整建制倒戈與改旗易幟者，說明這不是兩種制度間乾淨的界線，而是一場所有人都可能移動的內戰。
peopleEn: The decisive figures divide cleanly between the two sides. Carlos, Prince of Spain, was the nominal leader, but in the early years the field was actually run by General Tomás de Zumalacárregui, a veteran of the Peninsular War who had served in the French army before coming over to the Carlists, and who won his battles through discipline and mobility. He swore to uphold the fueros of Navarre, was proclaimed commander-in-chief of Navarre, and the provincial assemblies of Biscay, Álava and Gipuzkoa then pledged obedience to him; he made the Amescoas mountains his headquarters, and by one account three thousand volunteers with no resources at all came to swell his forces. Zumalacárregui was wounded in the leg by a stray bullet during the siege of Bilbao; the wound never healed properly and he died in August 1835, and his death was the hinge on which the northern situation turned. The Carlist ranks also drew in a crowd of foreign adventurers and writers: the Englishman C. F. Henningsen served as his chief bodyguard and later wrote his biography, while Prince Schwarzenberg, Prince Felix Lichnowsky and several dozen other Europeans fought in Spain, and about two hundred and fifty foreign volunteers, mostly French monarchists, enrolled with the Carlists. The pivot of the Liberal side was the regent María Cristina and the child queen Isabella II; in Madrid the government passed from Cea Bermúdez to Martínez de la Rosa and then to the Count of Toreno. Among the generals, Vicente Genaro de Quesada and Marcelino de Oraá Lecumberri were veterans of the Peninsular War and of the wars of South American independence, Jerónimo Valdés had fought at Ayacucho, Leopoldo O'Donnell added his own weight, and the man who finally turned the northern front was Espartero, whose swarming columns drove the Carlists out of the north. On the Carlist side Rafael Maroto was the crucial man, for it was he who signed the peace of 1839 on behalf of Don Carlos, while in the east Ramón Cabrera and the Carlist commanders of the Maestrazgo held out to the last. Across the whole war there were units that changed sides wholesale and men who swapped flags, which shows that this was not a clean line between two systems but a civil war in which anyone might shift.
kits: 卡面上的輪發槍是十六世紀的後膛手槍，到一八三〇年代在西班牙軍中已是老舊的象徵性裝備：機械昂貴、上弦與擊發緩慢、夜間還要維持慢火繩供火，一支可用的武器只配給軍官侍衛與王家衛士，自由派各團的作戰手槍早已改用燧發式，卡洛斯派則大量使用獵槍。這一點直接決定了它在戰役中的位置：北方山區的實際交火，靠的是火繩槍與獍槍配合的火槍、獵槍，以及從政府軍繳獲的燧發步槍。雙方步兵主力是燧發滑膛步槍，西班牙步兵普遍裝備口徑約十七毫米的滑膛槍，即俗稱「褐貝絲」式的舊式步槍，法國外籍兵團與葡萄牙常備師各用本國的單發前裝步槍，騎兵用軍刀、卡隆槍與長矛，卡洛斯派只有少量在城鎮鑄造的四磅與六磅鐵炮，數量遠少於政府軍的青銅制式炮，也沒有攻城重炮。雙方都沒有鐵路與火車，後勤完全靠獸力：卡洛斯派用騾隊沿山徑運糧，政府軍靠道路與徵糧車隊維持大城市與前線基地；卡洛斯派在歐納提鑄造銅錢，用以支付游擊隊的薪餉；海上力量方面，卡洛斯一方只有數艘小型帆船與走私船，用來把軍火從法國邊境運進比斯開沿岸。總括而言，兩邊的兵器差距並不大，真正的差距在於隊形、訓練與補給，而不在火器本身。
kitsEn: The wheellock pistol on the card is a sixteenth-century hand gun, and by the 1830s it was already an obsolete status object in the Spanish army: the mechanism was expensive, cocking and firing were slow, and at night the slow match still had to be kept alight, so a working example was given only to officers' servants and to the royal guard, while the hand guns of the liberal line regiments had long since been converted to flint, and the Carlists carried hunting guns in large numbers. That fact fixes the weapon's place in the campaign: the real shooting in the northern mountains was done with matchlock muskets, with hunting guns, and with flint muskets taken from government troops. The infantry backbone on both sides was the flintlock smoothbore musket; Spanish infantry generally carried smoothbore muskets of about seventeen millimetres, the old pattern popularly called a brownbess, while the French Foreign Legion and the Portuguese regular division used their own single-shot muzzle-loading muskets, and the cavalry used sabres, carbines and lances. The Carlists possessed only a few four- and six-pounder iron guns cast in the towns they occupied, far fewer than the liberal bronze ordnance, and no heavy siege artillery at all. Neither side had railways or locomotives; the whole of the logistics ran on animal power. The Carlists moved grain along mountain paths on mule trains, the government army kept the big cities and forward bases alive with roads and requisition convoys, the Carlists struck copper coin at Oñati to pay the bands, and their sea power was a few small sailing vessels and smuggling boats used to run arms in from the French frontier along the Biscayan coast. In sum, the gap between the two sides in weapons was not large; the real gap lay in formation, training and supply, and not in the artillery of small arms.
tactics: 卡洛斯派以游擊戰對抗正規軍：兵力分散，分隊行軍，晝夜不定，專打政府軍縱隊與補給線的側翼，埋伏地點多在峽谷、隘口、橋樑與村舍之間。扎馬拉卡雷基在北方多次避免正面會戰，改以縱隊行軍與分割包圍，使政府軍先後在阿爾薩蘇瓦、奧里亞門迪、安多因等役失利；英國輔助軍團在阿拉班的山道上遭伏潰散，是卡洛斯派山地戰術最典型的一役，爾後英軍失去有效戰鬥力。卡洛斯派還有情報上的優勢：他們在戰區之內，山徑、牧道與鄉村消息網都由支持者經營，政府軍的縱隊只能在谷地行軍，而卡洛斯軍可以用騾隊沿山徑輸送兵力與糧食。政府軍的戰術則是十九世紀的典型：步兵縱隊行軍，進攻時展開成線形，列陣齊射，騎兵掩護兩翼，遇卡洛斯襲擊即收縮成方陣；圍城用壕溝、壕壘與攻城炮兵，圍困帕拉斯卡與比爾巴鄂都是長期封鎖加逐步逼近，試圖切斷卡洛斯派的山區補給，皇家海軍與英葡艦隊同時封鎖港口，阻止軍火上岸。埃斯帕特羅接掌北方戰線後，改以大縱隊快速打擊，強迫卡洛斯分隊接受決戰，一八三六年十二月底在盧查納取勝，一八三九年八月迫使卡洛斯派接受和談。
tacticsEn: The Carlists fought a war of partisans against a regular army. Their numbers were small, they marched in separate bands, they moved by day and by night, and they aimed at the flanks of government columns and at their supply lines, choosing to lie in wait in gorges, at mountain passes, near bridges and among village farmsteads. Zumalacárregui avoided pitched battle in the north again and again, preferring marches by separate columns and the piecemeal encirclement that brought the government army to grief at Alsasua, Oriamendi and Andoain. The defeat of the British Auxiliary Legion in the passes of Arlabán is the most typical example of that mountain warfare, and after it the British were no longer an effective fighting force. The Carlists also had the advantage in intelligence: they lived inside the theatre of operations, and the paths, the drove roads and the network of village informants were all in the hands of their supporters, so that government columns had to travel through the valleys while Carlist bands could shift men and grain along the mountain tracks with mule trains. The government fought the war with the orthodoxy of the nineteenth century: infantry marched in column, deployed into line to advance, fired in ranks, cavalry covered the flanks, and when the Carlists struck they closed into squares. Siege was conducted with trenches, saps and siege artillery; the blockades of Pamplona and of Bilbao were long attritional operations intended to cut the Carlists off from the mountain supply, while the Royal Navy and the British and Portuguese squadrons simultaneously closed the ports to keep arms from landing. Once Espartero took over the northern front he changed to fast, deep columns, forcing the Carlist bands to accept a set-piece action; he won at Luchana at the end of December 1836, and by August 1839 he had driven the Carlists to accept terms.
data: 可核對的數字有限，但大致輪廓清楚。開戰時西班牙全國人口約一千二百三十萬，每平方公里居住不足二十人，比歐洲其他國家稀疏得多，兵源與市場都有限，這正是卡洛斯派能以游擊隊伍拖住正規軍的條件。一八三三年政府軍在北方可用兵力不多，無法一次壓倒卡洛斯派，戰事因此拖成七年。一八三五年五月，比斯開的采邑與吉普斯夸幾乎全境落入卡洛斯派手中。一八三四年《四國同盟條約》之後，英國輔助軍團初期約七千人，法國外籍兵團與葡萄牙常備師合計數千人，一八三六年前英法葡三國在北方投入的部隊合計約在一萬人上下，其後英方逐步收縮。政府軍靠全國徵兵維持規模，屢次因欠餉與裝備落後而士氣低落；卡洛斯派則長期靠徵糧、徵馬、捐輸與自鑄銅錢維持開支，據說卡洛斯本人在最困苦的時候一天只靠一鍋煎薯果度日。物資消耗同樣巨大：政府軍為圍城與遠征投入大量青銅炮與攻城器材，北方戰線的城鎮物資在反覆攻守中被大量消耗，戰後地方財政枯竭，國庫為此舉債。救護極差，野戰醫院簡陋，據當時記錄，莫雷利亞戰役中政府軍傷者有四分之三在數日內不治；史料對雙方總傷亡的估計相差數倍，多半因當時統計混亂，因此只能說這是歐洲十九世紀最傷亡慘重的內戰，參戰兵員的總數遠超半島戰爭。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are limited, but the general outline is clear. At the outbreak the population of Spain was about 12.3 million, with fewer than twenty inhabitants to the square kilometre, fewer than in any other European country, so that both the supply of men and the size of the market were restricted; that was precisely the condition that let Carlist partisan bands pin down a regular army. In 1833 the government had few troops available in the north and could not crush the Carlists in a single stroke, which is why the war stretched out over seven years. By May 1835 the seigneury of Biscay and nearly all of Gipuzkoa had fallen to the Carlists. After the Quadruple Alliance treaty of 1834 the British Auxiliary Legion numbered about seven thousand men at first, and the French Foreign Legion and the Portuguese regular division together some thousands more; the British, French and Portuguese troops committed in the north came to roughly ten thousand men before the British began to reduce their commitment. The government kept the scale of its army up by conscription across the country, and suffered repeatedly from arrears of pay and from obsolete equipment that broke down the morale of the troops; the Carlists maintained themselves for years on requisitioned grain, horses, donations and their own struck copper coin, and Carlos himself in his hardest days is said to have lived on a single pan of fried potatoes a day. The material consumption was enormous as well: the government poured bronze guns and siege material into its sieges and expeditions, the stores of the northern towns were consumed again and again by the seesaw of assault and defence, local finances were exhausted afterwards, and the treasury borrowed to cover it. Medical care was dire and field hospitals were crude; according to the contemporary accounts, three quarters of the liberal wounded in the Morella campaign died within days. The estimates of total casualties on both sides differ by a factor of several, largely because the contemporary statistics are confused, so the only safe statement is that this was the bloodiest civil war of nineteenth-century Europe, fought with far more men than the Peninsular War.
cause: 起因是一八三〇年費爾南多七世廢除一八一三年的《王位繼承詔令》，把自己女兒伊莎貝拉二世放在弟弟卡洛斯之上，理由是王子不願把王位交給外國出身的王后。費爾南多七世於一八三三年九月三十日病逝，四歲的女兒即位，遺孀瑪麗亞·克里斯蒂娜出任攝政，她主持的自由派政府把一八二〇年自由主義革命留下的制度固定下來：一八三〇年的城鎮憲章、一八三四年恢復宗教裁判所的教令，以及對教會與貴族特權的削弱。卡洛斯派因此主張王位繼承被自由派篡改，把鬥爭說成傳統秩序與合法權利對自由派掌權的鬥爭，其核心訴求是教會權威、鄉村自治法規與地方特權的恢復。經濟層面上，一八二〇年代後期美洲殖民地的收入崩落、財政枯竭、糧價高企，使全國上下都對現狀不滿，軍隊長期欠餉，於是卡洛斯派在鄉間獲得大量志願者，連城市手工業者也因自由派廢除行會與裁撤冗官而倒向卡洛斯一側。歸根到底，這場戰爭既是王位繼承之爭，也是西班牙在自由主義與傳統之間的第一次大撕裂。
causeEn: The cause lay in the fact that in 1830 Ferdinand VII revoked the Pragmatic Sanction of 1813 and placed his daughter Isabella II above his brother Carlos, on the ground that the prince would not hand the crown to a queen of foreign birth. Ferdinand VII died on 30 September 1833; the four-year-old daughter succeeded, and the widowed María Cristina became regent. The liberal government she presided over fixed in place the institutions the liberal revolution of 1820 had left behind: the municipal charter of 1830, the papal bull of 1834 restoring the Inquisition, and the curtailment of the privileges of church and nobility. The Carlists therefore argued that the succession had been tampered with by the liberals, and framed the struggle as one of the traditional order and lawful rights against liberal usurpation, with the restoration of clerical authority, of the rural fueros and of local privilege as their core demands. On the economic side the collapse of American colonial revenue in the later 1820s, an empty treasury and soaring bread prices made the whole country discontented, and the armies went for long stretches without pay, so that the Carlists drew large numbers of volunteers from the countryside, while urban artisans, whose guilds and redundant offices the liberals had abolished, drifted the same way. In the last analysis the war was a dispute over the succession and at the same time Spain's first great tearing between liberalism and tradition.
impact: 影響遍及制度、財政與軍隊。一八三六年八月二十九日政府頒布法令，把巴斯克與納瓦拉的自治法規收歸中央，稅收與兵役改由國家統一處理；一八三九年十月中央與巴斯克各省達成的協議保留部分稅收與徵兵自治作為交換；一八四一年《雅瓜斯條約》把納瓦拉正式改為西班牙的一個省，地方自治問題此後在西班牙政治中一再重演，演成十九世紀末的巴斯克經濟問題與二十世紀的民族主義衝突。軍隊成為決定國事的政黨，埃斯帕特羅一八四〇年以總攝政身份登位，自由派與溫和派的將領爭奪政權，一八四一年他本人被自己手下的將領推翻，說明將軍政治已經成形，而這正是卡洛斯派得以在往後四十年裡一再捲土重來的原因。財政上，這場戰爭把國庫掏空，軍隊規模膨脹而無力裁員，工業與鐵路計劃全部停擺，經濟長期落後。外交上，英國自一八三六年起逐步退出，西班牙在歐洲被視為不可靠的國家，卡洛斯派也未能得到任何列強的正式承認。戰爭的痕跡直到今天仍在：北方鄉村的生產結構受損、卡洛斯派的地方精英與傳統被重組，而卡洛斯主義作為一種政治選項，在此後的卡洛斯戰爭中一再復辟。
impactEn: Its consequences ran through institutions, public finance and the army. On 29 August 1836 the government issued a decree bringing the fueros of the Basque provinces and Navarre under central control, with taxation and conscription unified by the state; in October 1839 an agreement between the centre and the Basque provinces kept a reduced share of taxation and military recruitment in local hands in exchange; and in 1841 the Yanguas treaty turned Navarre formally into a province of Spain. From then on the question of local self-government returned again and again to Spanish politics, growing into the Basque economic question of the late nineteenth century and into the nationalist conflicts of the twentieth. The army became a political force deciding the affairs of the state: Espartero became prime minister and regent in 1840, the generals of the liberals and the moderates fought over power, and in 1841 Espartero himself was overthrown by his own officers, which showed that military politics had taken root — and that is precisely why the Carlists were able to rise again and again over the following four decades. Financially the war emptied the treasury, the army was inflated and could not be demobilised, and every plan for industry and railways was set aside, leaving the economy behind for decades. Diplomatically Britain withdrew step by step from 1836, Spain was treated in Europe as an unreliable state, and the Carlists obtained no formal recognition from any great power. The traces of the war remain to this day: the productive structure of the northern villages was damaged, the Carlist local elite and its traditions were reshaped, and Carlism as a political option returned in the later Carlist wars.
result: 北方以一八三九年的《維加拉公約》收場，公約由自由派埃斯帕特羅與卡洛斯派將領拉法埃爾·馬羅托簽訂：卡洛斯派放下武器、接受大赦，卡洛斯親王放棄王位繼承權，換取家族名號與不追究既往，馬羅托解散「王國會議」並解除效忠卡洛斯的武裝，北方各教區改派忠於王室的官吏，雙方並同意按省分別協商自治法規，保留部分稅收與徵兵自治。一八三九年八月三十一日的「貝爾加拉擁抱」是這場和解最具象徵的一幕。東線並未同步停火：卡布雷拉在加泰隆尼亞與馬埃斯特拉戈繼續抵抗，直到一八四〇年五月三十日莫雷利亞失守，埃斯帕特羅進軍貝加，到同年七月卡洛斯派殘部才被逐入法國。戰爭以自由派在制度上獲勝、卡洛斯派在戰場上被平定收場，但雙方都沒有達到全部目標：卡洛斯派守住了鄉村傳統的部分權益，自由派則以常備軍與嚴厲的高壓維持統一，為此付出七年兵役、國庫耗盡與北方鄉村破壞的代價。
resultEn: In the north the war ended with the Convention of Vergara of 1839, signed by the liberal Espartero and the Carlist general Rafael Maroto: the Carlists laid down their arms and accepted an amnesty, Don Carlos renounced his claim to the throne in exchange for the titles of his family and for immunity from prosecution, Maroto dissolved the Royal Council and disbanded the armed units loyal to Carlos, the northern districts were given officials loyal to the crown, and the two sides agreed to negotiate the fueros province by province, keeping a share of taxation and recruitment in local hands. The Embrace of Bergara on 31 August 1839 is the most symbolic scene of that settlement. The eastern front did not stop with it: Cabrera kept fighting in Catalonia and the Maestrazgo until Morella fell on 30 May 1840, after which Espartero advanced to Berga and by July of that year the remaining Carlist forces had been driven into France. The war ended with the Liberals victorious in institutional terms and the Carlists beaten in the field, but neither side achieved all of its aims: the Carlists preserved part of the rights of the rural tradition, and the Liberals held the country together with a standing army and severe repression, paying for it with seven years of conscription, an exhausted treasury and a devastated northern countryside.
